Top on the '2025' list is two good examples from totally different genres: Kendrick Lamar (hip hop), and Billie Eilish (vocal-forward electronica). Are electronica and hip hop worse for this? topComments.author: jongjong
topComments.text: LLMs are bad for rating or scoring anything because they have the sensibilities of the average person. Unfortunately, the average person has poor taste. This is a tough one to explain because some people think the average person has good taste by definition. I used to think that way but over the years I've realized that a lot of what the average person likes is derivative 'slop' - This was true before AI and still true with AI. Once you start deducting points for lack of originality, you will realize that people have really poor taste... Very narrow taste. Most people literally consume trashy variations of the same thing over and over. We have to start deducting points for this because the more intelligent among us can't take it anymore! We're tired of being exposed to thousands of variants of the same slop... It might be sufficiently different to fool the average pleb's simple mind but to us it's like eating the exact same dish every meal of every day with different amounts of salt and pepper. This comes through when you ask an LLM to rate/score something. It's frustratingly conventional and not based on first principles thinking and it ADDS extra points for being derivative instead of SUBTRACTING as it should. We can see it play out in the workplace. LLMs have poor judgement. It's the one area where they lag behind.

topComments.author: visarga
topComments.text: In my own words - you can't calibrate confidence of a model without a calibration set. Confidence is relative to some labeled dataset, it is established on a set of buckets or intervals, and is population based, something you can't check for a single prediction. Assign per case, verified per population. I thought the way Jev was presented was sneaky - you can't say "we calibrated the model for you" and skip having a task. specific calibration set. They couldn't have known all our future tasks.

topComments.author: themgt
topComments.text: A story which may or may not be based on lived experience: one day a Sprite stops booting. JuiceFS is asking object storage for a chunk and getting a 404. We wanted to go fast, so we ran JuiceFS in writeback mode. It records a chunk in its metadata first and uploads the bytes after. If the machine is killed at any time between those two steps, the metadata points at a chunk that doesn’t exist. So we built a harness that drives fleets of Sprites through write, checkpoint, sleep, wake and restore, over and over, verifying every byte that comes back. We pointed it at 400 JuiceFS Sprites for about 5,000 cycles. A nonzero number of them permanently lost the ability to checkpoint. Well … fuck. Enter: the Sprites Block Device (SBD). It takes a bucket and presents it to the Linux kernel as a block device, over NBD. The Sprite formats that device as ext4 and mounts it, the same way you’d mount a disk on any Linux box. Duh. This blog has has a strange vibe like "the last BRAWNDO we made in a bathtub may or may not have killed some customers lmao, try NEW BRAWNDO 2.0 TODAY!" that I didn't realize could work for corporate messaging around an in-house CoW cloud filesystem.

jobs.text: I’m Chris, VP Engineering at Fazeshift. You’ll own meaningful problems from ambiguity through design, implementation, rollout, and production, and you’ll work directly with the people affected by what you build. What would be the most reliable way to preserve event ordering per match while still allowing different matches to be processed concurrently? infoqArticles.title: Study Finds AI-generated Code Fails to Boost Productivity Due to Downstream Bottlenecks
infoqArticles.description: A recent Harvard study of 718 firms, using the Jellyfish analytics platform, finds that although AI coding assistants and agents increase code volume, this does not translate into a corresponding increase in completed work, partly because AI-generated code increases the workload in later stages of development, particularly code review. By Sergio De Simone
infoqArticles.author: Sergio De Simone

infoqArticles.title: Presentation: Actors for Agents: Patterns for Production AI
infoqArticles.description: Manju Rajashekhar explains how the actor model solves the complex runtime challenges of production AI agents. By treating agents as distributed systems, he discusses state ownership, message passing, write-through state, and supervision boundaries to manage failures, continuations, and mutable execution graphs, moving agentic workflows beyond fragile demos to resilient architecture. By Manju Rajas
infoqArticles.author: Manju Rajashekhar

infoqArticles.title: Vercel Labs Open-Sources fx: A Zig Coding Agent Designed to Be Embedded
infoqArticles.description: Vercel Labs has released fx, an experimental open-source coding agent written in Zig. It runs as a CLI, a script component, or an embedded library, including a WebAssembly build. Early feedback questioned its model-agnostic claim and a name conflict with an existing tool. Vercel says the project is pre-1.0 and changing quickly. By Daniel Curtis
infoqArticles.author: Daniel Curtis

infoqArticles.title: Article: AI Changes the Data Interface, Not the Query Engine
infoqArticles.description: This article presents a disaster-recovery analytics workflow in which an AI agent generates constrained SQL or Python, DuckDB computes reproducible facts from Parquet, and the agent interprets the results. It explains the determinism split, replayable analysis, and four signals for deciding when an embedded engine is sufficient or a managed lakehouse is justified. By Peihao Yuan
infoqArticles.author: Peihao Yuan

infoqArticles.title: Harbor Adds Docker Sandboxes to Run Reproducible AI Agent Evals in Isolated MicroVMs
infoqArticles.description: Docker announced that Harbor, the open-source agent evaluation framework, now works with Docker Sandboxes. This change allows each evaluation task to run in its own microVM. So, instead of sharing a container, tasks are isolated for better performance By Claudio Masolo
infoqArticles.author: Claudio Masolo

infoqArticles.title: Developer Behind the AI-Built Adobe Clones Says They Are “Not Anywhere Close to Ready
infoqArticles.description: A developer used Claude Opus 5.5 to build open-source replacements for seven Adobe applications, promoted them across Reddit with a projection of roughly 100% parity within a month, then told Hacker News the project was not anywhere close to ready. Its own roadmap puts it at 45% ready for real work and 2,300 to 4,100 agent-hours from full parity. By Steef-Jan Wiggers
infoqArticles.author: Steef-Jan Wiggers

infoqArticles.title: eMudhra Intermediate CA Compromise
infoqArticles.description: Private keys for eight eMudhra intermediate CA certificates have been compromised, allowing attackers to forge certificates for any site. The keys were revealed due to low entropy, not through a known breach. Browsers blocked them using revocation lists, but other software had to remove the emSign ECC G3 root. Unpatched systems remain exposed to forged certificates, including client auth and mTLS.
infoqArticles.author: Chris Swan

infoqArticles.title: Netflix Bridges AWS IAM and Internal Identity with Workload Attestation
infoqArticles.description: Netflix has developed a workload attestation mechanism for Apache Spark jobs running on Amazon EMR. The design combines AWS IAM identity with signed claims from Netflix’s control plane before issuing short-lived internal X.509 certificates, allowing managed compute workloads to authenticate to internal services without directly injecting credentials. By Leela Kumili
infoqArticles.author: Leela Kumili

infoqArticles.title: Article Series: Agentic AI Architecture
infoqArticles.description: In this article series, we try to establish agentic AI architecture as a new type of software architecture that will likely dominate the industry for years to come. The articles, written by industry experts, cover various elements and aspects of agentic AI architecture. We aim to present the latest trends and developments shaping the new type of architecture as it enters the mainstream. By Rafał G
infoqArticles.author: Rafał Gancarz

infoqArticles.title: Presentation: AI is an Amplifier: Scale High Performance, Not Dysfunction
infoqArticles.description: Nathen Harvey shares insights from DORA research on AI adoption in software delivery. He explains why AI acts as an amplifier, how the DORA AI Capabilities Model drives outcomes, and why engineering leaders must evolve beyond bottlenecks like code reviews to achieve sustainable productivity, reduce delivery instability, and empower developers without burning out their teams. By Nathen Harvey
infoqArticles.author: Nathen Harvey

infoqArticles.title: Google SynthID Detector Simplifies Watermark Detection and Expands Support to Other AI Providers
infoqArticles.description: Google DeepMind announced the global availability of SynthID Detector, a tool designed to help identify AI-generated content, including media created using AI tools from SynthID partners such as OpenAI, NVIDIA, and Kakao, with Apple support expected soon. By Sergio De Simone
infoqArticles.author: Sergio De Simone

infoqArticles.title: Article: Distributed Spring Batch Without a Message Broker
infoqArticles.description: Distributed Spring Batch partitioning already needs a shared, persistent job repository. This article makes that database the whole coordination plane and drops the message broker, sizing work to the live node count, a per-job master with no standing coordinator, compare-and-set claiming that prevents double-execution, two-phase heartbeat failover, and where a broker is still the right choice. By
infoqArticles.author: Janardhan Reddy Chejarla

infoqArticles.title: Cilium 1.20 Expands Gateway API and Opens eBPF Datapath for Kubernetes
infoqArticles.description: Cilium 1.20 has been released with broader Kubernetes Gateway API support, an extensible eBPF datapath and further work on sidecarless mutual TLS. The release also makes the newer netkit network device easier to introduce across Kubernetes fleets that run different Linux kernel versions. By Matt Saunders
infoqArticles.author: Matt Saunders

infoqArticles.title: Microsoft Previews dotnetup: Toolchain Manager for .NET SDKs and Runtimes
infoqArticles.description: Microsoft has released a public preview of dotnetup, a cross-platform toolchain manager that installs and updates .NET SDKs and runtimes in the user’s own directory without admin rights. It tracks channels such as latest, lts, preview, and daily, reads global.json, and removes unused installs. Commands may still change before general availability. By Almir Vuk
infoqArticles.author: Almir Vuk

infoqArticles.title: TornadoVM 7 Enables GPU-Native Workloads from Java Applications
infoqArticles.description: TornadoVM, an open-source heterogeneous programming framework for Java, has reached version 7.0. It automatically accelerates Java programs on multi-core CPUs and GPUs and provides a rich GPU programming ecosystem in Java that can be used with any mainstream JDK distribution e.g. Temurin, Red Hat OpenJDK, Coretto, Oracle, GraalVM or Zulu. By Ben Evans
